disposition_reason: Master of Public Health thesis evaluating a portable XRF screening method against GFAAS using 45 lead-fortified candy-matrix samples; it reports no lead concentrations in unspiked market candy, and its Table 1 quotes other agencies' data.

study.design: Method evaluation with spiked (fortified) candy matrix
study.market: candies obtained from merchants, vendors and volunteers in Clark County, Nevada (range-finding screen only)
study.method: Portable XRF (bulk sample and plastics modes) compared with GFAAS; FDA ICP-MS on initial samples (March 2008)
study.lod_text: XRF method detection limits 5.45 ppm (bulk sample mode) and 7.05 ppm (plastics mode), from 45 fortified analytical portions
study.qa: Fortified analytical portions 2.0-75.0 ppm lead and a candy-matrix method blank; spiked samples are not findings

regulatory_or_exposure.what: US FDA guidance level for lead in candy cited

unresolved: Range-finding XRF screen of about 30 candy brands is reported only as categories (high, medium, low, no lead), not as concentrations.
Table 1 (candies above regulatory limits, 2007-08) quotes other sources and is not extracted.
